messages:
Alex: Quick sync — attaching this week's GPU demand forecast and hot spots. Sheet: https://docs.redwood.ai/spreadsheets/forecast-2026. TL;DR: EU demand +12% WoW, US-West steady, APAC spiky around nightly model tests. Need decisions on burst pools and canary limits for next 72h. Thoughts?
Sana: Looked at the sheet — eu-west clusters trending 88% baseline. Two racks in eu-west1 show increased retransmits, upstream provider flagged brief packet drops (small but recurring). If partner trial hits, we'll lose headroom fast.
Miguel: FYI I'm scheduled to patch NIC firmware on eu-west1-b tomorrow 02:00 UTC (reduces available GPUs by 16 for ~3h). I can delay the window if we need capacity.
Alex: Don't clash with the canary window. Can we use Dedicated burst credits or spin quantized instances? What's the expected cost?
Priya: Cost quick-check: shifting 4 standard GPUs from reserved pool into burst for 7 days ≈ +$9,200. Short-lived quantized instances for heavy inference jobs could cut that to ~+$3k. Recommend throttling non-prod evals first.
Noah: Non-prod throttle is at 20% but devs keep launching long eval runs during EU daytime. I'll add a hard limit on runs >4h to the scheduler.
infra-bot: auto-alert — eu-west1 network jitter spike detected at 2026-03-25T14:12Z. p95 latency +42ms. Ticket created: INC-4521.
Sana: Also flag: partner trial scheduled Tue 18:00-02:00 UTC (48h window). If they run full throughput, estimate ~150k extra GPU-hours across EU+US over 48h. That will spike queue latency and may force autoscale into expensive burst.
Alex: Proposal: 1) Shift 6 GPUs from us-west overflow to eu-west for the trial window, 2) Enable lightweight model fallbacks (quantized variants) for non-SLA traffic, 3) Request preemptible quota bump in APAC overnight. Vote?
Miguel: +1 for 1 & 2. Preemptible quota bumps can take ~24h; if we need capacity faster we can temporarily run on-prem nodes in our lab cluster.
Priya: Approved. Finance note: if we absorb full partner load and use burst, upper estimate +$22k for the window. With throttles & fallbacks the likely cost is <$6k. I'll add both numbers to the sheet.
Alex: Actions: Miguel — postpone NIC patch to Thu 03:00 if we keep the canary; Miguel — prep 6-GPU shift playbook; Noah — enforce eval runtime cap and push short runbook to #devs; Priya — update finance tab; Sana — confirm partner run time and final spike numbers. I'll update forecast and notify leadership. :white_check_mark:
Noah: On it. I'll also push a small metric check to our forecasting job so we can see real-time burn during the window. Example query I'll add to the runbook:
```
# show queued jobs > 1h by cluster
kubectl get pods -n inference --field-selector=status.phase=Running -o json | jq '.items[] | {name: .metadata.name, cluster: .metadata.labels.cluster, runtime: .status.startTime}'
```
Priya: Also — small ask: tag any partner trial runs with `partner=trial-0426` so we can backfill chargebacks.
Sana: I'll coordinate with partner and confirm whether they want burst or a scheduled pace. If they accept paced run we avoid burst entirely.
Miguel: I'll hold off on the NIC patch until we confirm. If we need the on-prem nodes I'll ping infra on-call.
Alex: Thanks all. I'll send the exec summary once the partner confirms. If we get go-ahead, execute shift at Tue 17:30 UTC.
Noah: Will post a 1-page checklist in #eng-infra before handoff.
